environment.description: Same Kubernetes deployment but fronted by an AWS Application Load Balancer configured as Ingress (aws-load-balancer-controller). The ALB target group uses IP mode routing to the pod. The ALB listener on port 443 has a fixed-response default action (403). A forward rule exists ONLY when the request presents a valid client certificate from the internal PKI (ACM PCA arn:aws:acm-pca:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate-authority/ca-abc123). The ALB's mutual TLS mode is set to 'verify' with trust store arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:truststore/ts-internal/abc123. Additionally, a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricts ingress to the pod exclusively from the aws-load-balancer-controller's CIDR (VPC subnet 10.0.48.0/20), and the pod's service account has an IAM role with a condition key `aws:PrincipalTag/mtls-verified` that must equal 'true' for any AWS API calls the deploy scripts make.

config.alb_mutual_tls: verify mode, trust store ts-internal backed by ACM PCA ca-abc123
config.alb_listener_rule: forward to target group ONLY on successful mTLS handshake; default action is fixed-response 403
config.network_policy: ingress allowed only from 10.0.48.0/20 (ALB ENI subnet)
config.client_cert_issuer: ACM Private CA (RSA 2048, validity 1yr, CRL enabled)
config.certificate_revocation: CRL distribution point checked by ALB trust store every 60s
